definitions.explanation: Loanword from French, often implies a stylish or trendy establishment.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧カフェ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦コーヒー→コーヒー：00789_koohii⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}んだ→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
examples.english: I had coffee at the cafe in front of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{街|まち}→街：17306_machi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦おしゃれな→おしゃれ：02515_oshare⟧カフェ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There are many stylish cafes in this town.

examples.japanese: ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧カフェ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{待|ま}ち{合|あ}わせ→待ち合わせ：07397_machiawase⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I met up with a friend at a cafe.

notes:
カフェ is a loanword from French "café," referring to a coffee shop or similar establishment. In Japanese it typically implies a modern, stylish atmosphere.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- カフェ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go to a cafe
- カフェ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{過|す}ごす→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧: to spend time at a cafe
- カフェ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{勉強|べんきょう}→勉強：00770_benkyou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to study at a cafe
- カフェ⟦{巡|めぐ}り→巡り：noentry⟧: cafe hopping

TYPES OF CAFES IN JAPAN:
- ⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧カフェ: cat cafe
- ブックカフェ: book cafe
- メイドカフェ: maid cafe
- ⟦{古民家|こみんか}→古民家：11833_kominka⟧カフェ: cafe in a renovated traditional house

CONTRAST WITH ⟦{喫茶店|きっさてん}→喫茶店：01079_kissaten⟧:
カフェ suggests a trendy, modern space, often serving light meals and desserts. ⟦{喫茶店|きっさてん}→喫茶店：01079_kissaten⟧ evokes a traditional Japanese coffee shop with a quieter, more old-fashioned atmosphere. Both serve coffee, but the connotation differs.
